title: dynamic batching: sequence-length bucketing and padding-minimization heuristics (v4)
author: Evan Brooks
description:
Context: mixed-length workloads (chat + short prompts + long completions) cause excessive padding and KV-cache fragmentation in our continuous batcher. This PR introduces a lightweight, data-driven sequence-length bucketing strategy plus a padding-minimization hook that reduces wasted tokens while preserving latency SLOs. Motivation: reduce per-token cost and improve throughput in production workloads without large runtime changes or new configuration surfaces.

What this change does (high level):
- Add seqlen bucketing module that builds lightweight histograms and derives bucket boundaries using a configurable percentile heuristic (default: 10, 40, 70, 90) to capture common sequence-length modes.
- Within each bucket, batcher pads to the bucket's max length instead of the global max; a padding-minimization hook attempts to coalesce similar remaining-token requests before padding up.
- Add a small kernel selection hint that prefers lower-overhead attention kernels when the padded length falls into known quantization-friendly sizes.
- Reduce KV-cache fragmentation by keeping cache shards keyed by (model, bucket_id) and providing a TTL-based compaction to avoid unbounded growth.
- Backwards-compatible: runtime uses the new heuristics only when enable_seqlen_bucketing=true in BatcherConfig; default is enabled for dedicated deployments after canary.

Implementation notes:
- runtime/batching/seqlen_bucket.py contains the bucketing logic and histogram summarizer. It keeps a bounded reservoir (2k samples) per route and uses exponential decay to adapt boundaries.
- continuous_batcher.cpp: integrates bucketing decisions into the existing batching loop with minimal critical-path allocations; padding done via in-place vector resize.
- kernel_selector.cpp: small heuristic to prefer kernel A for padded-size <= 512 and kernel B otherwise. No kernel implementations changed.
- kv_cache_manager.py: add bucketed shard keys and a compaction job that runs every 5 minutes.

Checklist
- [x] Unit tests for bucket boundary selection and padding behavior
- [x] Integration test: mixed-length scenario with canary harness
- [x] Benchmarks: local perf harness + benchmark-canary run in CI
- [x] Docs: perf guideline and configuration docs updated

Results from benchmark canary:
- Tokens/sec (prod-like mix): +12% median across canary machines
- Padding tokens (waste): -22% measured on replayed query traces
- p50 latency: -6% on heavy long-seq traffic; p95: neutral (+1-2% in rare spikes)
- KV-cache entries: peak reduced ~18% due to coalescing and compaction

Rollout plan: start as a canary on dedicated and a small percentage of hosted routes (opt-in), monitor cost and qualitative regression signals from Redwood Optimize, then enable by default for Dedicated after 2 weeks of canary health.

Related: ENG-1724 (dynamic-batching roadmap), ENG-1830 (kv-cache compaction), SUP-4001 (customer report of high p95 on mixed workloads).

review_comments: Asha: Can you clarify how bucket boundaries adapt to diurnal patterns? Evan: we use exponential decay on the reservoir and recompute boundaries every minute; added note to docs.

Miguel: Are we sure kernel hints won't cause regressions on quantized models? Evan: hints are conservative and opt-in; we ran quantized-model canaries and saw no regressions; added unit test for kernel hint fallback.
Kara: NVMe-backed KV-cache compaction could impact IO; Evan: compaction is TTL+rate-limited and runs off the critical path; added metrics and a safety cap to avoid IO storms.
Miguel: pls add a feature flag path for hosted so we can roll back quickly. Evan: added enable_seqlen_bucketing flag and documented config for hosted toggles.

p50 latency -6% on long sequence workloads; p95 within +2%
KV-cache entries peak -18% due to bucketed shards and compaction
release_notes: Smarter sequence-length bucketing and padding-minimization reduces wasted tokens and improves throughput for mixed-length workloads. No public API changes. Configurable via BatcherConfig.enable_seqlen_bucketing.
